answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to pass a slow, verifiable delay puzzle bound to one non-transferable credential before joining a market, so creating thousands of fakes costs thousands of sequential delays, not one parallel computation. Honest agents build attested work over time, forming an oasis of trusted counterparties, while an operator flooding the network must pay the delay again for each dune of fake accounts it plants. A comet of new identities cannot outrun that cost curve, because the puzzle, credential, and history cannot be copied or bought in bulk.
